events.description: Expert Today, Expired Tomorrow? Solving Real Problems With AI What happens when the thing you spent years becoming really good at starts changing because of AI? You learn another AI tool. Then another one. Then an update arrives. Then someone tells you there is a better model. Then another tool appears. And suddenly, instead of doing your actual job, you feel like you are studying for an exam that never ends. Sound familiar? The truth is, you probably do not need to learn every AI tool. You need to learn how to use AI to solve real problems. Join us for Expert Today, Expired Tomorrow? Solving Real Problems With AI, a small and practical AI community meetup hosted by The AI Collective Kuala Lumpur Chapter in collaboration with Infosyte Sdn Bhd. This intimate session brings together professionals, creators, researchers, business leaders and curious minds in Kuala Lumpur for an honest conversation about AI, work, adaptability and what it means to stay relevant as technology keeps changing. No AI hype marathon. No endless list of tools you will forget by Monday. Just useful conversations, practical examples and people trying to figure out how to work better with AI. Why this conversation matters AI is changing how people research, create, communicate, analyse information and build their professional identities. events.description: Following the success of Flagright’s first financial crime handbook, the new Global Handbook for AI in Financial Crime Compliance asks how far AI can go in fighting financial crime, and how you defend every decision it makes. Malaysia has never needed the answer more. Online commercial crime nearly doubled in 2025, with almost RM3 billion lost. Police flagged more than 50,000 mule accounts in 2024. RMiT already requires behavioural risk profiles for every customer and checks on transfers to suspected mules. But by the time money reaches a mule, the scam has already worked. Every mule was a normal account once, and criminals plan the whole chain, from the scam that takes the money to the accounts that move it. What could AI catch if it thought like a criminal? To help answer that, we are joined by Malaysia’s leading crime prevention expert, Dr. Shamir Rajadurai , founder of Prevent Crime Now, who will open the morning with a talk on how criminals actually plan and run these operations, followed by a fireside chat on what that means for catching mules early. Join fraud, AML, and compliance leaders from Malaysian financial institutions for breakfast, a panel, and a live demo of AI catching a mule.
